active_themes.label: Warsh's Cut Dilemma
active_themes.summary: Hammack's hike warning remains uncontested and is now the dominant policy narrative. Warsh's credibility for cutting into 3.4% inflation with flat demand growth has collapsed. The Fed is publicly fractured. When Discover, Capital One, or Amex announce tightening (expected within 3-7 days), markets will reprice the cost of rate cuts and equity valuations will reset down 3-5 days after that announcement.

active_themes.label: Ceasefire Holds Near-Term
active_themes.summary: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announced today provides tactical breathing room. Iran-US hostilities remain unresolved. Oil closed modestly up but nowhere near spike. If Iran-US negotiations collapse in the next 72 hours, oil targets $95+. If a formal deal materializes, Warsh gets a 2-3 week reprieve but does not escape the core problem: rate cuts into stagflation.

active_themes.label: Lender Silence Narrows Window
active_themes.summary: Discover, Capital One, and Amex had clear cover to announce tightening today (flat spending, stagflationary pressures) and stayed silent. The window for this silence to hold is now 3-7 days, narrowing daily. When the first major lender announces, equity repricing accelerates. Their continued silence through Friday would signal belief that weakness is transitory—a bet contradicted by the macro data.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Officially Dead
active_themes.summary: May's 0% MoM spending combined with today's institutional silence removes all remaining soft-landing narrative credibility. Equities have not repriced this yet. The repricing cycle begins when the first lender announces tightening, expected in the next 3-7 days.

active_themes.label: Yields Stuck at Stagflation Range
active_themes.summary: 10-year remains 3.9-4.1%; 30-year at 2007 highs. Hammack's warning and today's spending data validate stagflation scenario. Yields will not move lower without hard demand destruction (not evident) or inflation rollover (not happening). This is the correct price for an economy cutting rates while inflation stays elevated.

active_themes.label: Bond Market Ahead of Equities
active_themes.summary: Bonds have correctly priced Warsh's policy error (rate cuts into 3.4% inflation, flat demand). Equities have not. The Nasdaq's 0.09% decline today is insufficient repricing. The reset comes when credit tightening is announced and becomes undeniable.
